subject.title: Agent declared tools != effective session tools: no strict inheritance mode, no visibility, no clipping reason trace

question: Should OpenClaw keep runtime clipping authoritative and add diagnostics first, or add a default-off strict inheritance mode that fails closed when declared and effective tools diverge?
rationale: The request changes the boundary between declarative agent config and lower runtime/session security layers, and it adds config/protocol surface in an area where repository policy requires explicit security and product direction.

options.title: Diagnostics First
options.body: Expose declared, effective, and removed tools with structured reasons while keeping sandbox, subagent, ACP, and runtime-host clipping authoritative.

options.title: Default-Off Strict Parity
options.body: Add a strict inheritance option that fails the session when declared and effective tools diverge, with explicit override-layer reporting and upgrade tests.

options.title: Document Existing Clipping
options.body: Keep current behavior and document that declared agent tool config is never final authority over session/runtime restrictions.

recommendation.title: Diagnostics First
recommendation.body: Expose declared, effective, and removed tools with structured reasons while keeping sandbox, subagent, ACP, and runtime-host clipping authoritative.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the best available owner signal for a cross-cutting config/runtime/security decision after recent capability-profile work in the affected path.
